name: Pennsylvania
standard: WCAG 2.1 A and AA minimum plus Revised Section 508 (ITP-ACC001 Digital Accessibility Policy, effective 2025-11-12)

laws.cite: Executive Order 2016-06, Enterprise Information Technology Governance
laws.summary: Gives the Office of Administration authority to issue IT policies, including the accessibility ITP.

laws.cite: 28 CFR Part 35, Subpart H (ADA Title II web/mobile rule, 2024; compliance dates extended by DOJ IFR effective 2026-04-20)
laws.summary: Requires state and local government web content and mobile apps to conform to WCAG 2.1 AA, with compliance dates now 2027-04-26 (population 50,000+) and 2028-04-26 (smaller entities and special districts).

applies_to: Offices, departments, boards, commissions and councils under the Governor, and any entity connecting to the Commonwealth Network. Local governments are covered only by the ADA Title II floor.

deadlines.what: ADA Title II floor: state government and local entities with population 50,000+ must conform to WCAG 2.1 AA (extended from 2026-04-24 by the 2026 DOJ IFR).
ADA Title II floor: local entities under 50,000 population and special district governments (extended from 2027-04-26).
ITP-ACC001 exempts Commonwealth social media posts made before this date.

requires: Agencies fund accessibility testing and remediation
OA Office of Accessibility tracks compliance and consolidates reporting to executives
Delivery Centers test with Commonwealth-approved tools and build remediation plans and roadmaps
Suppliers submit an ACR on the current VPAT version with bids and contracts
Archived content provided in accessible format on request
mobile: implied — covers all digital content and services and applications; mobile apps not named in the extracted text.
procurement: Contracts must require WCAG 2.1 A/AA; suppliers submit an ACR on the latest VPAT and must explain any older template.
enforcement: Internal governance via OA Office of Accessibility (RA-OAAccessibility@pa.gov); no public complaint procedure in the ITP; ADA Title II complaints to US DOJ.
notes: Replaces the 2025-07-29 version. The linked Digital Accessibility Standard was not opened.
